page_title: Choose Your Own Adventure Presentations with Reveal.js, Python and WebSockets

summary.title: Choose Your Own Adventure Presentations with Reveal.js, Python and WebSockets
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Reveal.js slide deck served by Flask that tallies audience SMS votes via Twilio and pushes live counts to the slides over WebSockets to pick the next slide.
takeaways: Set up a Flask project with Reveal.js templates and static files to serve a browser-based presentation.
Expose the local server with Ngrok and point a Twilio number's messaging webhook at the Flask app.
Store SMS 'left' or 'right' votes as counters in Redis and reply with a confirmation message.
Use Flask-SocketIO to emit vote counts to the browser so results update without a page refresh.
The companion GitHub repository has tagged steps (tutorial-step-1 to tutorial-step-3) to compare against.
summary.summary: This is a three-part Twilio blog tutorial by Matt Makai that walks through building a Choose Your Own Adventure style talk. The app uses Reveal.js for slides, Flask for serving pages and handling the Twilio SMS webhook, Redis for vote storage, and Flask-SocketIO to push live tallies to the browser. It covers project layout, configuration via environment variables, exposing localhost with Ngrok, and wiring up the vote counting and websocket updates. A GitHub repository with the final code and step tags is linked.
